events.description: China customs data on the gap between exports and imports, usually released without a fixed time in the first week of the month. June's surplus was the second largest on record, driven by surging chip and AI data centre hardware related exports; the release is watched for whether that export strength has been sustained into July, with knock on relevance for the Australian and New Zealand dollars.

The Cabinet Office's composite gauge of indicators, such as job offers and stock prices, designed to signal the direction of the Japanese economy a few months ahead. A useful but rarely market moving cross check on the broader growth picture the Bank of Japan is watching.

The Japan Machine Tool Builders' Association's early estimate of new orders for machine tools, a proxy for capital spending intentions in the manufacturing sector both at home and among export customers such as China. A niche but closely watched gauge of global industrial demand.

events.event: German industrial production and trade balance (June)
events.description: Destatis figures on output from Germany's factories and mines, released alongside the trade balance. As the Eurozone's largest economy and biggest exporter, German industrial data is watched as a bellwether for the currency bloc's manufacturing recovery and for how tariff related trade frictions are showing up in the numbers.

The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs' quarterly survey of Swiss household sentiment on their own finances and the wider economy. A gradual improvement would support the case that the SNB's ultra low rate setting is cushioning domestic demand even as the export sector struggles with franc strength.

events.event: Canada Labour Force Survey: employment and unemployment rate (July)
events.description: Statistics Canada's monthly labour market report, covering the change in employment and the jobless rate. Released alongside the US jobs report, it is watched for signs of how much slack is building in the Canadian economy while the Bank of Canada weighs the timing of its next move.

events.event: US Nonfarm Payrolls, average hourly earnings and unemployment rate (July)
events.consensus: around 85,000-95,000 jobs on average, though bank estimates range from roughly 40,000 to 120,000; average hourly earnings seen around +3.5% y/y; unemployment rate steady at 4.2%
events.description: The US Department of Labor's monthly employment report, the single most closely watched release on the calendar. June's payrolls figure of just 57,000 was well below expectations and reopened debate about the timing of the Fed's next move; a second soft print in July would add to that debate, while a strong number would support the more hawkish tone struck by some FOMC members at July's meeting.

Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin comments on the economy, arriving just hours after the July jobs report. As a regional Fed president, his reaction to the data and his framing of the path ahead are watched for clues on how the Committee's centre of gravity is shifting after July's split decision.

The Richard Ivey School of Business's seasonally adjusted survey of purchasing managers across Canada, covering activity, employment, prices and inventories. A secondary release compared with the Labour Force Survey out the same morning, but still watched as a timely, broad based read on Canadian business activity.

The Federal Reserve's monthly measure of outstanding credit card and other consumer borrowing. Watched for a gradual slowdown as a sign of how stretched US household finances have become after several years of high borrowing costs, though it is typically a low impact release.

A Cabinet Office survey of workers in consumer facing jobs, such as taxi drivers and retail staff, on near term economic conditions. Regarded as a well timed, real world sentiment gauge that feeds into the Bank of Japan's assessment of domestic demand.

A monthly survey of roughly a thousand investors and analysts gauging both current conditions and expectations for the Eurozone economy. Released earlier in the month than the more closely watched ZEW survey, it offers an early, sentiment based read on the currency bloc's growth outlook, though it is usually only a minor mover for the euro.

The British Retail Consortium's monthly tracker of like for like store and online spending, released ahead of the official ONS retail sales figures. An early, partial read on UK consumer demand that can move sterling at the margin if it diverges sharply from recent trend.

National Australia Bank's monthly survey of business sentiment and conditions. Released the day before the RBA's decision, it is watched closely for any last minute shift in the domestic backdrop that could tilt the Board's language.

events.event: RBA interest rate decision and Statement on Monetary Policy
events.description: The Reserve Bank's Monetary Policy Board decision, released alongside the quarterly Statement on Monetary Policy that carries the Bank's updated growth and inflation forecasts. A Reuters poll found all 37 economists surveyed, and all four major Australian banks, expect a hold at 4.35%, though a number still flag the risk of one further hike later in 2026 given elevated inflation, so the tone of the statement matters more than the rate itself.

Governor Michele Bullock's press conference following the rate decision. Traders parse the Governor's language on the inflation and growth outlook for hints on whether the Board still has room to raise the cash rate again or has reached the peak of the current tightening cycle.

events.event: South Africa Quarterly Labour Force Survey (Q2)
events.description: Stats SA's quarterly survey of employment and unemployment, one of the most closely watched domestic releases for the rand given South Africa's persistently high jobless rate. The Q1 reading marked a jump to 32.7%, so this update is watched for whether the labour market weakness has continued into the second quarter.

The National Federation of Independent Business's monthly survey of small business sentiment on hiring, sales and pricing plans, usually released on the second Tuesday of the month. A useful cross check on the health of Main Street businesses, though typically a secondary mover for the dollar.

events.event: German Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, final (July)
events.description: The final, confirmed reading of Germany's HICP inflation figure, the measure used for comparison across the euro area and a key input into the ECB's policy thinking. It rarely diverges from the flash estimate, but as the bloc's largest economy, any surprise revision can move the euro at the margin.

Statistics Canada's forward looking measure of planned construction activity, based on permits issued by municipalities. A useful, if volatile, early signal for the housing sensitive parts of the Canadian growth outlook.

The Bureau of Labor Statistics' inflation report, the most closely watched US data release of the week, due at 8.30am Eastern time. Headline CPI has been reaccelerating in recent months as the conflict driven jump in oil prices around the Strait of Hormuz feeds into energy costs, keeping the Fed under pressure to balance its inflation fight against signs of labour market cooling. A hot print would bolster the hawkish minority on the FOMC, while a softer one would support the case for the Fed to look through the energy spike and keep open the door to a near term rate cut.

events.event: RBNZ Survey of Expectations: two year inflation expectations (Q3)
events.description: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's quarterly survey of businesses and forecasters on where they expect inflation to sit two years out. Two year expectations climbed to 2.53% in the second quarter from 2.37% in the first, so this update is watched for whether that upward drift has continued, since a further rise would narrow the RBNZ's room to ease policy.

The Office for National Statistics' first estimate of UK economic growth for the second quarter, published alongside the June monthly GDP figure. GDP grew 0.6% in the first quarter, so this reading is the key gauge of whether that momentum has been sustained; a stronger than expected print is generally supportive for sterling, while a miss adds to the case for the Bank of England to keep policy accommodative.

events.event: UK trade balance, index of production and construction output (June)
events.description: Released alongside the GDP figures, this bundle covers the goods and services trade balance, manufacturing and industrial output, and construction sector activity for June. These are the underlying components that feed into the quarterly growth number and are watched for a more granular read on where UK momentum is coming from.

events.consensus: annual rate expected to ease from June's 5.5%, with some estimates near 5.1% or lower
events.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' measure of wholesale price pressures, released a day after CPI. June's headline PPI fell 0.3% on the month but was still up 5.5% on the year, and this report is watched for whether producer level inflation is cooling from that pace or if the energy driven price pressures seen in the consumer figures are also showing up further up the supply chain.

The Department of Labor's weekly count of new unemployment benefit claims, released alongside PPI. A high frequency, early read on the US labour market that typically has limited standalone impact but is watched closely for any signs of a sharper turn in hiring conditions following recent soft payrolls prints.
